findings.title: Registered metric-alert handler is now uninstantiable
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still the detector_handler for the registered MetricAlertFire group type, but it now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of the abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Instantiating it raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler constructs the class on access, and process_detectors does not catch that error, so a single metric_alert_fire detector aborts processing for the whole batch. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned an empty list.

findings.title: Occurrence hook cannot see the packet that fired
findings.body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is the new extension point for emitting an issue, but it only receives group_key, the numeric value, and the new priority. The DataPacket being evaluated is not passed through, nor is the previous DetectorStateData. A detector-specific occurrence (for example a metric alert) needs subscription id, timestamps, and other evidence that exist only on that packet. Implementers must stash the packet on the handler during get_dedupe_value or get_group_key_values, which is implicit and will force a breaking signature change as soon as a real subclass is written. Pass the packet into the hook.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], and process_detectors depends on that mapping, but the docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Callers following the docstring will iterate the dict keys (group keys) instead of the result values.

findings.title: Group-key evaluation test builds the expected occurrence for the wrong key
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with group_key "val1" (and value 6) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_fingerprint includes the group key, and IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, so the expected DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal the value under test. This test fails and does not lock the new occurrence hook.

findings.title: Occurrence helper ignores value, and several expectations pass the wrong one
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never puts it on the IssueOccurrence or event_data, so equality cannot tell whether evaluate forwarded the measured value into build_occurrence_and_event_data. Call sites also pass a value that does not match the packet: test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2=10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6 (line 191); test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6 (line 490); test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6 (line 510). A regression that dropped or swapped the value argument would still pass.
